response: Use four work units, exactly matching the four plan tasks. Dispatch them serially: Tasks 1-3 each go to a fresh mechanical implementer for the wording replacement in its one document and its focused test; Task 4 goes to a fresh high-judgment implementer for the concurrent funds-reservation and idempotency-key change and its focused tests. Do not combine the three similar documentation tasks and do not run any implementers concurrently: the baseline workflow requires a fresh subagent per task and explicitly forbids parallel implementation dispatches. Immediately after each implementer finishes, run that task's combined spec-compliance and code-quality review, and do not dispatch the next task until the current task passes its gate (or completes the prescribed fix loop). After all four task gates pass, run one broad whole-branch review. The mechanical tasks justify the cheapest implementation tier and proportionate reviewers; the concurrency/idempotency task warrants the deep implementation tier and a reviewer calibrated to its higher correctness risk; the final review uses the most capable reviewer because it evaluates cross-task branch quality. Assuming every review is clean, there are no fix rounds and no human stops.
